answer: Sybil resistance comes from requiring each identity to complete a verifiable chain of sequential modular squarings before it is accepted. A Wesolowski proof lets others verify the result efficiently, but does not remove the chain’s sequential dependency: GPUs cannot compress one identity’s required elapsed time through parallel computation. An attacker may run chains for several clones concurrently, yet each clone still incurs its own physical delay and computational cost—whether the identities are labeled violet, inlet, or orchard.
